headline: CALABARZON Minimum Pay Rises October 26, Including ₱750 Kasambahay Increase
seoTitle: CALABARZON Wage Increases Take Effect October 26
seoDescription: Private-sector minimum wages rise by up to ₱45 daily and the kasambahay floor rises by ₱750 monthly across CALABARZON on October 26.
deck: New regional wage orders set private-sector daily floors at ₱550 to ₱645 and the domestic-worker monthly floor at ₱7,500.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The CALABARZON regional wage board approved increases of up to ₱45 a day for minimum-wage workers in the private sector, effective October 26. The increase is equivalent to as much as ₱1,170 a month for a worker paid on 26 workdays.
A separate order raises the regional monthly minimum for kasambahays by ₱750 to ₱7,500. DOLE estimates that about 201,000 domestic workers will benefit.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The National Wages and Productivity Commission lists new private-sector minimum rates ranging from ₱550 to ₱645 a day under Wage Order IVA-23. The precise increase depends on the industry and the classification of the city or municipality where the worker is employed.
The domestic-worker increase is governed by Wage Order RB-IVA-DW-06 and applies across Batangas, Cavite, Laguna, Quezon and Rizal.

sections.heading: Why it matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The increase raises the legal pay floor in one of the country’s largest industrial regions. Workers should check the official wage matrix because not every employee receives the full ₱45 adjustment, and existing lawful pay above the minimum is not automatically increased by the same amount.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for the final published wage matrices, employer compliance after October 26 and DOLE guidance on exemptions, complaints and correction of wage distortion.
